question: What is the main job of haustrations (pocket-like folds) in the colon?

options.A: Adding digestive juices to the food mixture
options.B: Speeding up the travel time of liquid waste
options.C: Pushing stool directly out of the anus
options.D: Mixing food contents to help the body absorb water

explanation: Think of haustrations as gentle churning movements in the large intestine. They mix things up slowly so the bowel lining has enough time to soak up water and minerals! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h1)

question: How do mass movements differ from regular mixing movements in the large intestine?

options.A: Segmental movements require conscious effort to move waste.
options.B: Segmental contractions happen only once or twice a day.
options.C: Mass movements push stool a long way toward the rectum all at once.
options.D: Mass movements happen non-stop all day and night.

explanation: Mass movements are like big, powerful waves that sweep through the colon every now and then to clear out stored waste toward the exit. You've got this! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h1)

question: Which part of the nervous system controls the built-in (intrinsic) defecation reflex?
explanation: The enteric nervous system is essentially the 'brain of the gut.' It handles local reflexes all on its own without needing signals sent all the way from your head! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h2)

question: What is the main job of the lower spinal cord (sacral segments) during the parasympathetic defecation reflex?

options.A: Relaying stretch signals to boost colon waves and relax the inner valve.
options.B: Stopping all gut movement until you reach a restroom.
options.C: Producing slippery mucus to help stool slide out easily.
options.D: Giving the person conscious control to tighten the outer muscle.

explanation: When the rectum stretches, the lower spinal cord helps coordinate the action by ramping up colon squeezes and opening the inner pathway. Brilliant teamwork by the body! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h2)

question: What kind of muscle makes up the external anal sphincter?
explanation: Because the outer sphincter is made of skeletal muscle, you have voluntary control over it. It's what lets you hold it in until you reach a toilet! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h3)

question: What happens when stool enters the rectum and you decide to hold it in for a bit?

options.A: The gut nerves completely reverse the direction of the waste.
options.B: The voluntary outer muscle contracts to override the reflex.
options.C: The parasympathetic nerves shut down all feeling completely.
options.D: The involuntary inner valve tightens up even more.

explanation: You consciously squeeze your skeletal external sphincter to keep things in check when it's not the right time or place to use the restroom. Perfectly normal! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h3)

question: Why do people naturally perform the Valsalva maneuver (bearing down) when passing stool?

options.A: It increases pressure in the belly to help push stool out.
options.B: It prevents air from getting trapped in the large intestine.
options.C: It stimulates nerves to slow down a racing heart.
options.D: It forces the inner anal sphincter to snap shut tightly.

explanation: When you hold your breath and push (bearing down), your abdominal muscles tighten up and create the downward pressure needed to help empty the colon. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h4)

question: Which patient should be extra careful to avoid heavy straining and the Valsalva maneuver?

options.A: A patient with a mild cold or runny nose
options.B: A patient diagnosed with mild iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: A patient recovering from a recent heart attack (myocardial infarction)
options.D: A patient doing therapy for a sprained ankle

explanation: Straining spikes blood pressure and heart strain. For a patient healing from a heart attack, that extra stress can be very dangerous. Good clinical thinking! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h4)

question: What is the main reason a fecal impaction forms in the rectum?

options.A: Too much nerve stimulation in the lower spinal cord
options.B: Waste sitting in the bowel too long, losing all its water
options.C: Eating way too many high-fiber foods every day
options.D: Mass movements happening way too fast

explanation: If stool hangs out in the rectum for too long, the body keeps sucking water out of it until it turns into a hard, stubborn rock-like mass. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h5)

question: What is a great nursing action to help prevent constipation in a patient who just had surgery and is on bedrest?

options.A: Encouraging fluids and early walking as ordered
options.B: Applying hot water bottles directly to the lower belly
options.C: Giving a strong anti-diarrhea pill right away
options.D: Instructing the patient to stop eating all solid foods

explanation: Water softens the stool, and physical movement gets the bowels waking back up after surgery. Simple nursing care makes a massive difference! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h5)
